VI.TI,VA
The external female genitalia is called the vulva.
It contains independent openings of the urethra and
vagina. The sides of the vulva have two small fleshy
folds, the labia minora (lesser lips) which are hidden
by larger hairy folds, the labia majora (greater lips).
These folds are the equivalents of the male scrotum.
In the uppennost angle of the vulva in front of the
urethral opening is located, a small erectile clitoris
which is highly sensitive and is the equivalent of
male penis.
nVlDUCTS
The two oviducts, also called Fallopian tubes
or uterine tubes, are about 12 cm long. Near the
corresponding ovary, each oviduct has a funnel-shaped
opening called the oviducal funnel. Cilia lining the
funnel help to pick up and push the released ovum
into the oviduct. Subsequently, the waves of muscular
contractions (or peristalsis) of the wall of oviduct
push the egg down into the uterus.

an upper wider portion which receives the two

cervix or neck.

11 B. FROM FERTILISATION TO BIRTH
You have learnt about the different parts and their arrangement in the male and female
reproductive systems in the Section A of this chapter. Here, you will study how a new
individual is conceived and how it grows in the mother's womb and finally born as a
baby.
11.4 FERTILISATION (union of egg nucleus and
sperni nucleus)
During copulation (mating or coitus), the
Spern￿ are released in the vagina near the cervix
of the uterus. A single ejaculation by the human
male contains about four hundred million spernis.
These spenns actively swim with the help of their
tails (Fig. 11.4A) and pass through the cervix into
the cavity of the uterus progressing at a rate of
approximafrly 1.5 mm per minute. From the uterus,
they climb up. to reach the oviducts. If there

I. FRATERNAL TWINS (Produced from two ew)
Sometimes, two eggs are released from ovaries at a time and both may get fertilised to pr(xluce tivo individuals. Such twins
produced from two eggs are calledfraternal rwins. Fraternal twins may be either both boys, or both girls, or one boy and one girl.
Fraternal twins in all respects are like the norn￿1 sisters and brothers, but here they are of the same age having been born within a
few minutes of each other. About 75 cent of all cases of twins belong to this type. Fraternal twins are biologically known &$ .
Dlovular (meaning produced from two ova), or Dizygotic (meaning produced from two zygotes, that is. two fertilised eggs).
2. IDENTICAL TW￿s (Produced from one egg)
Sometimes, a single fertilised egg may get split and separated into two parts during its early stages of cell division. Each of these two
split parts then behaves like an independent egg and produces one complete individual each. Identical twins being produced from a
single egg are either both boys or both girls: and for the same reason, they are very similar (identical) to each other. YeL all is not
similar in identical twins, for example fmgerprints. birth marks and even halldwritin￿ are not similar.
MORE THAN TWO - THE TRIPLFTS, QUADRUPLETS, ETC.
Sometimes, three, four or even more babies are born from a single pregnancy. Such births may arise due to a variety of
conditions. for example
Triplets (three born at a time) may be produced either from one single zygote, splitting into two, and one of the split parts
again splitting into two, or the triplets may be pr￿UCed from two eggs in which one zygote produces a pair of identical twins
and the other develops nornially into one baby.
Quadruplets (four born at a time) may be produced as two pairs of identical twins from two eggs or in other combinations
of identical and fraternal twins.
